name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
title: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
answer: Deep research agents are software systems that carry out multi-step literature search, reading, and synthesis tasks, producing landscape scans that map a field's key papers, claims, models, tools, and open questions. A landscape scan is not a single search result but a structured overview built from many sources, often covering hundreds of papers and extracted claims. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,555 extracted claims is one example of the kind of corpus such an agent works from. These agents aim to reduce the time a competent researcher spends on manual screening while keeping the original paper as the unit of evidence.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Deep research agents are software systems that carry out multi-step literature search, reading, and synthesis tasks, producing landscape scans that map a field's key papers, claims, models, tools, and open questions. A landscape scan is not a single search result but a structured overview built from many sources, often covering hundreds of papers and extracted claims. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,555 extracted claims is one example of the kind of corpus such an agent works from. These agents aim to reduce the time a competent researcher spends on manual screening while keeping the original paper as the unit of evidence.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Deep research agents run on a mix of large language models, retrieval systems, and document parsers, usually orchestrated through an agent loop that plans queries, fetches pages, and stores notes. They depend on access to full-text papers, metadata, and citation graphs, often through institutional subscriptions or open repositories. The site's catalogue of 91 AI books, 801 scientific models, 732 AI tools, and 674 glossary terms suggests the breadth of entity types an agent must index and cross-reference. Compute is typically cloud-based, with model inference and embedding search as the main costs.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done in stages: the agent breaks a research question into sub-questions, runs searches across bibliographic databases and preprint servers, retrieves candidate papers, extracts claims and methods, and then clusters findings into themes. It compares claims across papers, flags contradictions, and builds a landscape map with nodes for papers, models, tools, and terms. Content on this site links to the original paper rather than to a search tool, so the agent's output must preserve a direct path from each claim to its source. Human review remains part of the loop, especially for judging study quality and relevance.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on provenance, citation accuracy, and the danger of hallucinated summaries or fabricated references. A deep research agent must record which paper each claim came from and link to the original, not to a secondary search interface. Licensing and access terms vary by publisher, so agents must respect paywalls and use only what the user is entitled to read. There is also a risk of over-trusting an agent's synthesis, so outputs should be treated as a map to the literature, not as a replacement for reading key sources.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Deep research agents are moving toward longer-horizon tasks, such as updating a landscape scan when new papers appear, comparing methods across subfields, and drafting evidence tables with confidence labels. They are likely to become more interactive, letting a researcher ask follow-up questions about a specific claim or cluster. The site's growing collection of extracted claims and models points toward a future where landscape scans are maintained as living documents rather than one-off reports. The main open problem is reliable claim extraction and contradiction detection across noisy, inconsistent paper formats.
